entry.title: NextAR & Vuzix
entry.content:
Bringing Augmented Reality Guidance Directly into the Operating Room

Case Study | Orthopedic Surgery, AR & Surgical Precision

Overview

In orthopedic surgery, precision is everything. Surgeons must visualize complex anatomical relationships while maintaining constant focus on the surgical field. Traditionally, this has required looking away at monitors, relying on assistants, or using bulky navigation systems—each adding friction, cost, or cognitive load.

NextAR, a surgical augmented reality platform developed by Medacta, partnered with Vuzix to bring real-time, patient-specific surgical guidance directly into the surgeon’s field of view using Vuzix Blade™ smart glasses. The goal: improve surgical accuracy, reduce distractions, and enhance outcomes without disrupting natural surgical workflow.

The Challenge

Orthopedic procedures—particularly joint replacements—require:

  • Accurate alignment and placement

  • Continuous visualization of biomechanical data

  • Minimal distraction during critical steps

  • Hands-free access to guidance

Traditional navigation systems often require:

  • Large capital equipment

  • Additional OR staff or operators

  • Surgeons to look away from the patient

  • Increased setup time and cost

Surgeons needed a way to access guidance without diverting their eyes or hands from the procedure.

The Solution: NextAR + Vuzix Smart Glasses

NextAR created a see-through augmented reality surgical platform that overlays patient-specific guidance directly into the surgeon’s natural line of sight using Vuzix Blade smart glasses.

How It Works

  1. Pre-operative planning

    • CT scans are processed through proprietary algorithms

    • A personalized biomechanical model is created for each patient

  2. Intra-operative AR guidance

    • Surgeons wear Vuzix Blade smart glasses

    • Real-time guidance appears directly over the patient

    • Alignment, angles, depth, and positioning data are displayed live

    • Surgeons never need to look away from the surgical field

The result is a seamless fusion of digital intelligence and real-world anatomy.

Designed for the Operating Room

Vuzix Blade smart glasses were selected specifically for surgical environments because they are:

  • Lightweight and comfortable for long procedures

  • Hands-free, with voice commands for interaction

  • See-through, preserving full situational awareness

  • Durable and ergonomic, designed for all-day wear

As Dr. Wes Cox, Orthopedic Shoulder & Elbow Surgeon and Section Chief at UAMS Orthopaedics, explains:

“Having Vuzix glasses gives you the truth. Immediately you know that not only is this what you intended to do, but this is what you’re about to do.”

Zero Distraction, Maximum Focus

One of the most critical advantages of the NextAR platform is cognitive simplicity.

Surgeons do not need to:

  • Look at external monitors

  • Shift attention away from the patient

  • Rely on verbal cues from others

Instead, all relevant information appears exactly where and when it’s needed, allowing surgeons to maintain continuous focus on the operative field.

As Dr. Cox noted, after a brief learning curve, using the glasses feels no different than normal surgery—except with “extra real-time feedback.”

Clinical Benefits

The NextAR + Vuzix solution delivers meaningful advantages:

Improved Surgical Accuracy

  • Patient-specific biomechanical models

  • Real-time tracking and alignment feedback

  • Reduced variability between planned and actual outcomes

Reduced OR Complexity

  • No bulky navigation towers

  • No additional equipment operators

  • Lower setup time and footprint

Enhanced Training & Education

  • Surgeons can see exactly what they’re doing, with immediate feedback

  • Ideal for teaching complex procedures

  • Visual learning accelerates skill acquisition

Expanding Across Specialties

While initially focused on orthopedic joint replacement, the NextAR platform is now being used across multiple surgical specialties, including:

  • Shoulder replacement

  • Knee replacement

  • Spine procedures

The same AR-driven approach adapts to different anatomical models and surgical workflows.

The Future of AR in Surgery

According to Dr. Cox, augmented reality has enormous potential beyond guidance alone:

  • Improved surgical education

  • Real-time collaboration

  • Better communication with anesthesiology and OR staff

  • Lower hospital costs by reducing reliance on large navigation systems

He emphasizes that AR doesn’t replace surgical skill—it enhances it, allowing surgeons to make better decisions with greater confidence.

Conclusion

The collaboration between NextAR and Vuzix demonstrates how augmented reality can be seamlessly integrated into real surgical workflows. By delivering real-time, patient-specific guidance directly into the surgeon’s field of view, the solution improves precision, reduces distraction, and elevates both surgical performance and education.

This case study shows that AR-guided surgery is no longer theoretical—it’s already improving outcomes in operating rooms today.

entry.title: Fujitec & Vuzix
entry.content:
Remote Audits and Field Service Support with Smart Glasses

Case Study | Industrial Services, Maintenance & Remote Support

Overview

Maintaining and servicing large-scale elevator and building systems requires highly skilled engineers, strict safety standards, and precise documentation. For global companies like Fujitec, which designs, installs, and services elevators and escalators worldwide, ensuring consistent service quality across regions is both operationally complex and resource-intensive.

To address these challenges, Fujitec deployed Vuzix M400 smart glasses to support remote audits, maintenance, and field service operations—enabling hands-free, real-time collaboration between field engineers and remote experts.

The Challenge

Fujitec faced several interconnected challenges common to industrial service organizations:

  • Increasing complexity of equipment maintenance

  • Limited availability of highly experienced engineers

  • Time-consuming travel for audits and inspections

  • Difficulty scaling expert support across many sites

  • Need for consistent, high-quality service delivery

Traditional approaches required senior engineers to travel frequently to job sites, which reduced productivity and slowed response times. At the same time, less-experienced field engineers needed better access to expert guidance when handling complex or unfamiliar issues.

The Solution: Vuzix M400 Smart Glasses

Fujitec evaluated multiple smart glasses solutions and ultimately selected Vuzix M400 smart glasses for full-scale deployment.

Why Vuzix

Fujitec chose the Vuzix M400 because of its:

  • Hands-free operation, critical for safety and efficiency

  • High-quality, real-time video streaming

  • Long battery life suitable for full workdays

  • Durability in harsh, on-site environments

  • Compatibility with helmets and protective equipment

  • Ease of use for engineers in the field

After several proof-of-concept evaluations, Fujitec moved forward with a broad rollout.

How the System Works

  • Field engineers wear Vuzix M400 smart glasses during maintenance or inspection work

  • When additional support is needed, they initiate a live video connection

  • Remote experts see exactly what the engineer sees in real time

  • Experts provide step-by-step guidance, verification, and troubleshooting

  • Audits and inspections are completed remotely, without travel

This “see-what-I-see” capability allows Fujitec’s most skilled engineers to support multiple field teams simultaneously.

Remote Audits & Inspections

One of the most valuable applications has been remote audits.

Using smart glasses, Fujitec can:

  • Conduct audits hands-free and in real time

  • Verify compliance with maintenance standards

  • Capture visual documentation digitally

  • Reduce the need for travel to remote or international sites

This ensures consistent quality while significantly reducing inspection costs and delays.

Improved Productivity & Workforce Utilization

By deploying smart glasses, Fujitec enabled its teams to:

  • Resolve issues faster in the field

  • Reduce downtime caused by waiting for on-site experts

  • Allow senior engineers to focus on higher-value tasks

  • Increase overall productivity by completing additional work ahead of schedule

The solution allows engineers to use saved travel time to complete more maintenance and service tasks, directly increasing operational efficiency.

Business Impact

The deployment of Vuzix smart glasses delivered clear operational benefits:

  • Faster issue resolution and service response

  • Reduced travel time and costs

  • More efficient use of skilled engineering resources

  • Improved consistency in audits and service quality

  • Scalable remote support across regions

Smart glasses became a core tool in Fujitec’s maintenance and service workflow—not just a temporary solution.

Conclusion

Fujitec’s adoption of Vuzix M400 smart glasses demonstrates how augmented reality can modernize industrial maintenance and field service operations. By enabling hands-free remote audits and expert support, Fujitec improved productivity, reduced costs, and ensured consistent service quality across its global operations.

This case study shows how smart glasses help industrial organizations scale expertise, protect safety, and operate more efficiently in complex environments.

entry.title: MERGE Solutions & Vuzix
entry.content:
Improving Operating Room Efficiency with Remote Surgical Support

Case Study | Healthcare, Surgery & Augmented Reality

Overview

Operating rooms are among the most complex and high-cost environments in healthcare. Even small inefficiencies—delayed start times, unnecessary room traffic, or overcrowding—can significantly impact patient safety, infection risk, and hospital costs.

MERGE Solutions, a healthcare technology company focused on surgical efficiency, partnered with Vuzix to deploy smart glasses–enabled remote surgical support. The goal was to reduce operating room congestion, improve communication, and give surgeons real-time access to critical expertise—without requiring additional people in the room.

The Challenge

Modern surgeries often require the presence of Medical Device Representatives (MDRs) to provide guidance on specialized instruments and implants. Traditionally, this meant:

  • MDRs physically present in the operating room

  • Increased OR traffic and door openings

  • Higher infection risk

  • Delayed start times when reps were unavailable

  • Increased operational costs

During surgery, OR staff must work in a sterile environment with limited access to external information. Once doors close, doctors and scrub techs are isolated and must rely solely on their own knowledge—even when remote expertise could help.

MERGE identified the need for a solution that could:

  • Provide real-time MDR support without physical presence

  • Reduce OR congestion

  • Improve efficiency and decision-making

  • Maintain strict sterility standards

The Solution: Smart Glasses–Enabled Remote MDR Support

MERGE Solutions implemented Vuzix M400 smart glasses combined with secure video conferencing and augmented reality tools.

How It Works

  • Surgeons or scrub techs wear Vuzix smart glasses during procedures

  • A remote Medical Device Representative joins virtually

  • The MDR sees exactly what the surgical team sees

  • The MDR provides live guidance on instruments, implants, and workflows

  • Images, videos, data, and solutions can be delivered directly into the wearer’s field of view

The remote MDR becomes a virtual participant, observing surgery from a first-person perspective without entering the operating room.

Why Smart Glasses Matter in the OR

Smart glasses were critical because they:

  • Keep hands completely free

  • Preserve an unobstructed surgical field of view

  • Eliminate the need for handheld devices

  • Reduce cognitive load during procedures

  • Maintain a sterile environment

Unlike tablets or monitors, guidance appears exactly where it’s needed—within the surgeon’s line of sight.

Key Benefits in the Operating Room

The solution delivered multiple operational improvements:

Reduced OR Congestion

By removing the MDR from the operating room, overall OR occupancy decreased.

Result:

  • 17% reduction in OR occupancy after removing the MDR from the room

Improved Surgical Efficiency

Remote MDRs could:

  • Monitor multiple video feeds during live surgery

  • Provide timely guidance before, during, and after procedures

  • Support multiple surgeries in parallel

This reduced delays and improved start times.

Lower Infection Risk

Fewer people entering and exiting the OR meant:

  • Fewer door swings

  • Reduced post-operative infection risk

  • Better adherence to sterile protocols

Reduced Operating Costs

With remote participation:

  • Fewer on-site staff were required

  • MDRs could support more surgeries without travel

  • Hospitals reduced staffing and operational expenses

Digital Documentation & Implant Tracking

MERGE also digitized implant documentation:

Before MERGE

  • Implant usage was recorded manually with paper and pencil

  • Data was handed off to nursing staff

  • Billing and reconciliation were slow and error-prone

After MERGE

  • Implant usage is recorded digitally during surgery

  • Records are synchronized with the hospital, surgeon, and device manufacturer

  • Invoicing is faster and more accurate

This eliminated manual steps and improved financial workflows.

Results (as of 2023)

The program delivered measurable, real-world results:

  • 280 surgeries performed using smart glasses technology

  • 3 surgeons, 20 scrub techs, and 5 medical device reps actively involved

  • Software and workflows refined to improve OR efficiency and consulting quality

  • At least one full person removed from the OR per surgery

  • 17% reduction in OR occupancy

  • MDR involvement reduced to 20–40% of total surgical time, while still providing full support

Business Impact

With Vuzix smart glasses, MERGE Solutions enabled hospitals to:

  • Improve OR efficiency and utilization

  • Reduce infection risk

  • Lower operating costs

  • Improve surgical communication and outcomes

  • Scale expert support without adding physical staff

Remote MDRs can now provide expert consultation while:

  • Supporting other surgeries

  • Working from other hospitals

  • Even assisting while traveling

Conclusion

The MERGE Solutions and Vuzix collaboration demonstrates how augmented reality can meaningfully improve surgical operations. By transforming MDRs into virtual participants, hospitals reduce congestion, improve efficiency, and maintain sterility—without sacrificing expertise or care quality.

This case study shows that smart glasses are not just a convenience in healthcare—they are a powerful operational tool for modern operating rooms.

entry.title: University of Rochester & Vuzix
entry.content:
Bringing Mixed Reality Surgical Training into the Operating Room

Case Study | Medical Education, Surgery & Mixed Reality

Overview

Surgical training has traditionally relied on in-person mentorship, observation, and repetition—methods that are increasingly difficult to scale. As procedures grow more complex and healthcare systems face staffing shortages, educators are searching for new ways to train surgeons effectively without compromising patient safety.

At the University of Rochester Medical Center, faculty recognized that mixed reality (MR) could play a transformative role in surgical education. In collaboration with Vuzix and Help Lightning, the university deployed Vuzix M4000 smart glasses to create a mobile mixed-reality surgical training platform designed specifically for use in the operating room (OR).

The Challenge

Surgical training environments present unique constraints:

  • Surgeons must keep their hands completely free

  • Any obstruction to the natural field of view is unacceptable

  • Cognitive load during procedures must remain minimal

  • Traditional devices (tablets, monitors, handheld cameras) disrupt workflow

  • Remote mentorship is difficult to implement safely in the OR

At the same time, surgeons in training need:

  • Real-time guidance

  • Visual context from expert mentors

  • Opportunities to practice without putting patients at risk

The University of Rochester needed a solution that could deliver remote expertise, real-time visual guidance, and hands-free operation—all while meeting strict clinical standards.

The Solution: Mixed Reality with Vuzix Smart Glasses

The University of Rochester adopted Vuzix M4000 smart glasses, paired with surgical software and Help Lightning’s remote collaboration platform, to deliver mixed-reality training directly inside the OR.

Why Smart Glasses

Smart glasses were selected because they:

  • Preserve the surgeon’s full, unobstructed field of view

  • Allow hands-free access to guidance and overlays

  • Enable real-time, first-person video sharing

  • Maintain natural surgical posture and workflow

Unlike handheld devices, the glasses allow trainees to remain fully focused on the procedure while receiving expert input.

How the System Works

  • A trainee surgeon wears Vuzix M4000 smart glasses during a procedure

  • A remote mentor surgeon sees exactly what the trainee sees

  • Text, image, and visual overlays can be added in real time

  • The mentor guides the trainee step-by-step during the procedure

  • Feedback is immediate, contextual, and intuitive

This creates a mixed-reality training environment where the trainee’s field of view and the mentor’s guidance are combined into a single, seamless experience.

Zero Cognitive Burden, Maximum Learning

One of the most critical benefits is the elimination of cognitive overload.

By fusing:

  • The trainee’s real surgical view

  • The mentor’s hands, guidance, and overlays

the system allows surgeons to learn without shifting attention, checking external screens, or breaking sterile focus. Guidance appears exactly where it’s needed, when it’s needed.

As faculty emphasized, even a brief interruption or obstructed view in surgery can have serious consequences—making this hands-free, see-through approach essential.

Applications Beyond Live Surgery

The University of Rochester also uses the platform for:

Surgical Simulation & Training

  • Trainees practice on ultra-realistic 3D-printed anatomical models

  • Models are created using patient CT scans and imaging data

  • Both dissolvable and non-dissolvable materials replicate real tissue behavior

  • Surgeons can rehearse complex procedures before operating on patients

Remote Mentorship & Education

  • Experts can mentor surgeons from anywhere in the world

  • Training continues even when travel is impossible

  • Knowledge transfer scales without geographic limits

The Role of Help Lightning

Help Lightning’s AR-enabled remote assistance software enhances the experience by:

  • Allowing mentors to work virtually “side-by-side” with trainees

  • Supporting real-time collaboration without visual obstruction

  • Integrating seamlessly with Vuzix M4000 hardware

Together, the hardware and software create a mobile mixed-reality surgical platform that functions safely inside the operating room.

Why It Matters

The University of Rochester’s approach addresses several critical needs in modern healthcare:

  • Better-trained surgeons entering the operating room

  • Higher-quality assistance during complex procedures

  • Increased access to subject-matter experts

  • Scalable surgical education without travel

As remote learning becomes essential across healthcare, this model ensures training quality does not decline—in fact, it improves.

The Future of Surgical Practice

Faculty at the University of Rochester see mixed reality extending far beyond training alone.

They envision a future where:

  • Every surgeon has access to expert assistance on demand

  • Remote collaboration spans hospitals, regions, and countries

  • Even experienced surgeons can receive support during difficult cases

  • Surgical outcomes improve through shared expertise

As one surgeon noted, no matter how skilled you are, there are always cases where collaboration makes the difference.

Conclusion

The University of Rochester’s deployment of Vuzix M4000 smart glasses demonstrates how mixed reality can safely and effectively transform surgical education. By enabling hands-free, real-time mentorship directly in the operating room, the program improves training quality, expands access to expertise, and enhances patient safety.

This case study shows that the future of surgical training—and surgical collaboration—is already here.

entry.title: CH Four Biogas & Vuzix
entry.content:
Driving Savings with Remote Construction Audits

Case Study | Energy, Construction & Remote Inspection

Overview

Like many companies during the COVID-19 pandemic, CH Four Biogas® had to rethink how critical work was performed when travel restrictions made on-site visits difficult or impossible.

CH Four Biogas is a leading producer of anaerobic digestion and renewable energy installations across North America. As the company scaled its operations, frequent, time-intensive field inspections became a major constraint—both in cost and in the number of projects the company could support simultaneously.

To overcome these challenges, CH Four Biogas deployed Vuzix M400 smart glasses to conduct remote construction audits and inspections, significantly reducing travel, saving time, and improving operational efficiency.

The Challenge

CH Four Biogas’ plant construction operations depend on frequent on-site inspections to:

  • Ensure contractual obligations are met

  • Verify construction milestones

  • Track progress across multiple job sites

  • Respond quickly to unforeseen issues

Before the pandemic, engineers traveled to project sites four to five times per quarter, often crossing the U.S.–Canada border. A single trip to a rural job site could take 3–5 days, consuming valuable engineering resources and limiting the number of projects the company could take on.

Travel restrictions in 2020 made this approach unsustainable.

The Solution: Remote Construction Audits with Smart Glasses

CH Four Biogas turned to Vuzix M400 smart glasses to enable remote, “see-what-I-see” inspections using augmented reality.

How It Works

  • On-site personnel wear Vuzix M400 smart glasses

  • Remote engineers connect via a mobile Wi-Fi hotspot

  • Engineers see exactly what’s happening on site in real time

  • Remote experts guide inspections, commissioning, and troubleshooting

  • Issues are identified and addressed immediately

This approach allows precise, efficient inspections without requiring engineers to travel.

As CH Four Biogas explains:

“Describing something on a call or email can only go so far. Our engineers need to see what’s going on in real time. The see-what-I-see capability of the glasses meant we had eyes on the ground.”

Time- and Labor-Intensive Inspections, Reimagined

A typical installation project can span 2–3 years, with active construction lasting 6–12 months. Traditionally, an engineer would need to be on site multiple times during this period.

With Vuzix smart glasses:

  • Critical payment milestones can still be verified

  • Security oversight is maintained even during restricted periods

  • Engineers can remotely inspect, commission, and troubleshoot

  • Multiple projects can be monitored simultaneously

Remote engineers can virtually “walk” sites across North America in a single day.

Measurable Cost Savings

The financial impact was immediate.

  • $70,000 USD saved in travel costs during pandemic restrictions alone

  • Significant reductions in time spent per inspection

  • Better utilization of senior engineering staff

  • Increased project capacity without increasing headcount

Keeping a pair of Vuzix M400 smart glasses at remote sites allowed a single senior engineer to support multiple installations at once.

Operational & Client Benefits

Beyond internal savings, the solution delivered additional advantages:

  • Faster response to construction issues

  • Improved project timelines

  • Reduced carbon emissions from travel

  • Clients benefit from lower inspection costs

  • Greater flexibility during highly restrictive periods

As Lapointe of CH Four Biogas notes:

“We’re able to be in multiple places at once and vastly extend the power of our limited staff.”

Forward-Looking Strategy

Remote inspections are now central to CH Four Biogas’ growth strategy.

By eliminating the need to send inspectors to every installation, the company can:

  • Scale operations across North America

  • Support more projects simultaneously

  • Reduce overall carbon emissions

  • Maintain high inspection quality

Smart glasses have become a foundational tool—not a temporary workaround.

Conclusion

CH Four Biogas’ adoption of Vuzix M400 smart glasses demonstrates how remote inspection technology can unlock major efficiencies in construction and energy infrastructure projects. By replacing travel-heavy audits with real-time remote collaboration, the company reduced costs, improved scalability, and strengthened its ability to deliver renewable energy installations on schedule.

This case study shows that remote construction audits are not just a pandemic solution—they’re a smarter way to operate.

entry.title: Ricoh Japan & Vuzix
entry.content:
Remote Support for Multi-Function Device Maintenance with Smart Glasses

Case Study | Field Service & Digital Transformation

Overview

As manufacturing and service organizations face growing labor shortages and an aging workforce, passing on technical expertise from veteran engineers to newer employees has become increasingly difficult.

Ricoh Japan, responsible for the sales and maintenance of Ricoh’s multi-function printers and related equipment, addressed this challenge by deploying Vuzix M400 smart glasses as part of its maintenance department’s digital transformation initiative.

The goal was to preserve institutional knowledge, improve service quality, and enable less-experienced customer engineers (CEs) to resolve complex issues faster—without requiring veterans to travel on-site.

The Challenge

Ricoh Japan operates at significant scale:

  • 4,600 customer engineers

  • 431 service offices nationwide

  • Thousands of customer visits per day

Like many service organizations, Ricoh Japan faced several challenges:

  • Difficulty hiring and onboarding new engineers

  • Aging veteran workforce with deep, hard-to-replace expertise

  • Inconsistent service quality across regions

  • Rising pressure to resolve issues faster

  • COVID-era constraints on travel and on-site staffing

While remote support had already been explored using digital tools, traditional solutions still required handheld devices and limited hands-free collaboration.

The Solution: Vuzix M400 Smart Glasses

Beginning in May 2021, Ricoh Japan deployed Vuzix M400 smart glasses to enable real-time, hands-free remote support during customer maintenance visits.

How It Works

  • A customer engineer wears Vuzix M400 smart glasses on site

  • If an issue is routine, the engineer resolves it independently

  • For complex or unfamiliar problems, the engineer connects to a remote expert at the service office

  • Using the built-in camera and microphone, the remote veteran sees exactly what the on-site engineer sees

  • The expert provides live guidance via audio and video

As Ricoh Japan’s Suzuno—himself a former CE—explains:

“It’s just like they’re standing right behind me, telling me how to handle it. With smart glasses, both your hands are free.”

Why Smart Glasses (Not Smartphones)

While smartphones could theoretically provide similar connectivity, Ricoh Japan found smart glasses far superior for field maintenance because they:

  • Keep both hands free during repairs

  • Provide a stable, first-person view

  • Reduce distraction during complex tasks

  • Improve safety and efficiency

Bluetooth earphones also ensure guidance from remote experts is not audible to customers, preserving professionalism on site.

Knowledge Transfer & Training Benefits

The system allows veteran engineers to:

  • Share decades of experience remotely

  • Support multiple field engineers without traveling

  • Train younger engineers while solving real customer issues

Less-experienced engineers benefit from:

  • Faster problem resolution

  • Real-time coaching in live environments

  • Accelerated skills development

This approach simultaneously improves service quality and shortens training timelines.

Security & Customer Privacy

Ricoh Japan implemented strict security and privacy guidelines for on-site use:

  • Customer permission is required before activating camera or microphone

  • Clear policies govern how video and audio are used

  • Smart glasses are highly visible, eliminating concerns about hidden recording

According to Ricoh Japan, customers have responded positively:

“Many customers appreciate that we’re using advanced tools, and that contributes to a better corporate image.”

Measurable Results

The deployment has already delivered tangible operational improvements:

  • On-site service times reduced by hours in some cases

  • Faster resolution of complex issues

  • Fewer required on-site visits by veteran engineers

  • Reduced personnel movement—critical during COVID-19

  • Improved consistency and quality of service nationwide

Ricoh Japan plans to continue expanding the program, with the long-term goal of equipping every young customer engineer with smart glasses.

Supporting Sustainability Goals

Ricoh Japan also views the initiative through the lens of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):

  • Quality Education (SDG 4): Training and upskilling junior engineers

  • Decent Work & Economic Growth (SDG 8): Enabling experienced engineers to work remotely

  • Industry, Innovation & Infrastructure (SDG 9): Modernizing maintenance operations

  • Reduced Inequalities (SDG 10): Equalizing support quality across regions

  • Climate Action (SDG 13): Fewer service trips, lower CO₂ emissions

Business Impact

By adopting Vuzix smart glasses, Ricoh Japan has:

  • Preserved critical technical knowledge

  • Improved service speed and quality

  • Reduced travel and operational costs

  • Enhanced customer confidence and brand image

  • Advanced its digital maintenance strategy

As Director Shimmyozu notes, this initiative is a cornerstone of Ricoh Japan’s broader digital transformation.

Conclusion

Ricoh Japan’s use of Vuzix M400 smart glasses demonstrates how remote support technology can modernize field service operations at scale. By combining hands-free collaboration with real-time expert guidance, Ricoh has improved service quality, accelerated training, and built a more resilient maintenance organization.

This is a practical example of how smart glasses are moving beyond experimentation—and becoming essential tools for modern service operations.

entry.title: Ohana One & Vuzix Full Case Study
entry.content:
Delivering Life-Saving Medical Coverage Globally Through Surgical Remote Assist

Full Case Study | Global Health & Medical Education

Overview

Around the world, access to safe and timely surgical care remains critically limited—especially in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). A global shortage of trained surgeons, combined with legal barriers, travel restrictions, and high costs, has made it difficult to deliver advanced surgical training where it is needed most.

Ohana One, a California-based nonprofit, recognized this challenge early. In partnership with Vuzix, Help Lightning, and TeleVU, Ohana One created a scalable remote surgical training and mentorship program that enables surgeons to receive expert guidance in real time—without leaving their home countries.

The result is the Surgical Sight Program, a technology-enabled model that expands global surgical capacity while keeping care local.

The Challenge

The shortage of trained surgeons is most severe in LMICs, where physicians often face:

  • Limited access to advanced surgical education

  • Lack of experienced mentors

  • Travel and visa restrictions

  • High costs associated with in-person training

  • COVID-19–related disruptions

Many surgeons must leave their communities to receive training, reducing already scarce access to care. Others never receive the advanced mentorship needed to perform complex procedures safely.

Ohana One identified the need for a remote, high-quality, and sustainable training solution that would allow surgeons to continue serving patients while advancing their skills.

The Vision

Ohana One’s mission is to bridge global gaps in surgical care by providing:

  • Access to advanced surgical training

  • One-to-one mentorship from expert surgeons

  • Innovative, easy-to-use technology

  • High-quality educational resources

The guiding principle is simple:
train surgeons where they live, so patients can be treated where they live.

The Solution: Surgical Sight Program

Ohana One launched the Surgical Sight Program, built around Vuzix M400 Smart Glasses and real-time collaboration software.

How the Program Works

  • Each participating surgeon receives a pair of Vuzix M400 smart glasses

  • Surgeons are paired with a volunteer mentor who is an established expert in their specialty

  • Using first-person “see-what-I-see” video streaming, mentors observe surgeries in real time

  • Mentors provide live guidance, feedback, and instruction during procedures

  • All interaction is hands-free, high-resolution, and individualized

This approach allows expert mentors to guide surgeons as if they were physically present in the operating room.

Technology Stack

The program combines:

  • Vuzix M400 Smart Glasses

    • Lightweight and comfortable for all-day use

    • Personal heads-up display for high-quality viewing

    • Hands-free operation for uninterrupted surgical workflow

  • Help Lightning and TeleVU software

    • Real-time video collaboration

    • Augmented reality overlays

    • Interactive “virtual presence” for mentors

Mentors can highlight areas on screen, guide incision placement, and assist with decision-making—creating a seamless, real-time teaching environment.

Clinical Applications

The Surgical Sight Program is currently active across multiple specialties, including:

  • Plastics and reconstructive surgery

  • General surgery

  • Colorectal surgery

  • Neurology and neurosurgery

  • OB/GYN

  • Orthopedics

The technology is used not only during live surgery, but also for:

  • Pre-surgical planning

  • Post-operative recovery and follow-up

  • Ongoing education and case review

Benefits for Surgeons and Patients

The program delivers immediate and long-term benefits:

For Surgeons

  • Access to expert mentorship regardless of location

  • Ability to perform more complex procedures safely

  • Faster learning and skill development

  • No need to leave their communities for training

For Patients

  • Improved access to advanced surgical care

  • Reduced need to travel long distances

  • Better outcomes through earlier intervention

  • Stronger local healthcare systems

Global Impact (as of late 2021)

The Surgical Sight Program has achieved measurable, real-world impact:

  • 95 surgeons onboarded and active in the program

  • 77 hospitals across six continents supporting Ohana One

  • 41 countries served, benefiting over 4.43 billion people

  • 1,664 life-changing services delivered through Ohana One’s international surgical aid since 2019

  • 44 full surgeries completed using Vuzix smart glasses with live mentor support

Why It Matters

Rather than extracting talent from underserved regions, Ohana One’s model builds capacity locally. Surgeons stay in their home countries, continue providing care, and gain advanced skills at the same time.

This approach creates a multiplier effect:

  • More trained surgeons

  • More patients treated

  • Stronger, more resilient healthcare systems

As Ohana One emphasizes, the outcome is straightforward:
more surgeons trained leads to more lives saved.

Conclusion

The collaboration between Ohana One and Vuzix demonstrates how wearable technology can fundamentally transform global healthcare education. By combining smart glasses with real-time mentorship, the Surgical Sight Program delivers advanced surgical training anywhere in the world—without borders.

This is not experimental technology. It is a proven, scalable solution already changing lives.

entry.title: Vuzix & Aptus (GSL)
entry.content:
Disrupting the Supply Chain with Pick-by-Vision Smart Glasses

Logistics Case Study

Overview

In the era of e-commerce and global shipping disruptions, supply chain operators face increasing pressure to move goods faster, more accurately, and at lower cost. Rising shipping expenses, import/export restrictions, and labor challenges have made traditional logistics processes more expensive and less resilient.

To meet these challenges, Global Shipping and Logistics (GSL) partnered with Aptus and Vuzix to deploy a pick-by-vision solution powered by smart glasses—transforming warehouse execution through augmented reality (AR).

The Challenge

Logistics and warehousing operations are under constant pressure to:

  • Increase speed and throughput

  • Reduce picking and processing errors

  • Maintain stability while scaling operations

  • Improve worker efficiency without compromising accuracy

  • Avoid costly traditional automation investments

Operators needed a solution that could improve productivity while remaining flexible, easy to adopt, and cost-effective.

Why Pick-by-Vision?

Pick-by-vision combines human vision with augmented reality, delivering instructions directly into a worker’s field of view.

As Gurumurthi Shankar, Chief Commercial Officer at GSL, explains:

“Humans are most comfortable using sight out of all five senses. Vision paired with minimal voice commands makes this an easy application to use and an overall easy technology to adopt.”

Compared to traditional automation, AR offers:

  • Greater flexibility

  • Faster deployment

  • Lower implementation cost

  • Reduced operational errors

The Solution

GSL implemented Vuzix smart glasses integrated with Aptus ExpertVision and the Manhattan SCALE Warehouse Management System (WMS).

Key Capabilities

  • Hands-free picking using vision-based instructions

  • Voice and visual guidance for task execution

  • Real-time decision support on the warehouse floor

  • Event recording for later review and analysis

  • Dynamic integration with existing WMS workflows

Workers receive pick instructions directly through the smart glasses interface, allowing them to work faster while keeping both hands free.

Technology Integration

Vuzix Smart Glasses

GSL selected Vuzix smart glasses because they combine:

  • Artificial Intelligence (AI)

  • Augmented Reality (AR)

  • Machine Vision

This combination delivers:

  • Real-time visual and audio references

  • On-the-spot decision-making support

  • All-day comfort and ease of use

The glasses also connect directly to GSL’s WMS, enabling workers to access inventory, shipping, receiving, and other business functions instantly.

Manhattan SCALE by Aptus

Aptus’ Manhattan SCALE WMS powers the backend of the solution, providing:

  • Inventory management

  • Picking and slot replenishment

  • Distribution optimization

  • Order planning and forecasting

  • Labor and billing management

  • RFID management

Existing scanner workflows and configurations remain intact. New picking flows are automatically pushed to the smart glasses, increasing flexibility without disrupting productivity.

Measurable Results

The deployment delivered previously unheard-of performance gains across key warehouse operations:

  • 15% performance increase in receiving, reducing average depalletization time by 4 minutes

  • 24% performance increase in put-away, reducing average slotting time by 22 minutes

  • 20% performance increase in picking, reducing average order processing time by 16 minutes

These gains were achieved without compromising quality or accuracy.

Business Impact

By deploying pick-by-vision smart glasses, GSL was able to:

  • Serve more customers at higher speed

  • Reduce costly operational errors

  • Improve workforce efficiency and satisfaction

  • Maintain flexibility during demand fluctuations

  • Avoid expensive traditional automation investments

The solution freed operators’ hands, simplified tasks, and delivered real-time guidance exactly when and where it was needed.

Conclusion

The collaboration between Vuzix, Aptus, and GSL demonstrates how augmented reality can fundamentally transform supply chain execution. Pick-by-vision smart glasses deliver the speed of automation with the flexibility of human decision-making—unlocking productivity gains without sacrificing accuracy.

As GSL notes, this is not science fiction. This is real, deployable technology delivering measurable results today.

entry.title: Vuzix & Chi Mei Medical Center
entry.content:
Transforming Emergency and Critical Care with Smart Glasses

2020 Case Study | Taiwan

Overview

The Chi Mei Medical Center in southern Taiwan is one of the region’s most advanced healthcare systems, operating three hospitals and serving both urban and rural populations. Known as an early adopter of cutting-edge medical technology, Chi Mei has consistently pioneered innovations in emergency care, robotic surgery, and precision medicine.

To further improve speed, collaboration, and patient outcomes—especially in time-critical situations—Chi Mei integrated Vuzix Smart Glasses into emergency, intensive care, and surgical workflows.

The Challenge

Emergency and critical care environments are defined by two factors: information and time.

  • Doctors must make rapid, high-stakes decisions

  • Specialists are often not physically present when needed

  • Information must be shared instantly across departments and facilities

  • Hands must remain free during treatment and procedures

Even short delays in stroke, cardiac, or trauma cases can mean the difference between life and death. Traditional communication tools—phones, handheld cameras, or monitors—were not sufficient for real-time collaboration in fast-moving clinical settings.

The Solution: Vuzix Smart Glasses

Chi Mei deployed Vuzix M-Series Smart Glasses to enable hands-free, real-time “see-what-I-see” communication across its healthcare system.

The glasses provide:

  • Full HD live video streaming

  • Two-way audio communication

  • Secure conferencing with specialists

  • First-person point-of-view visibility

All without interrupting patient care.

Use Case 1: Emergency Room Collaboration

In emergency situations, paramedics typically treat patients en route while ER teams wait for arrival. With Vuzix Smart Glasses, Chi Mei doctors can begin diagnosis and treatment before the patient reaches the hospital.

Key Benefits

  • ER physicians see exactly what paramedics see in real time

  • Doctors can assess consciousness, paralysis, trauma severity, burns, and aneurysm rupture remotely

  • Medical history, medications, and vital signs are shared instantly

  • Treatment planning begins earlier, saving critical minutes

Because Chi Mei operates satellite hospitals in rural areas, ER doctors at regional facilities can consult simultaneously with specialists at the main hospital in Tainan—deciding treatment priority and transfer timing while the patient is still in transit.

Use Case 2: Intensive Care Unit (ICU)

In Chi Mei’s ICU, attending physicians are responsible for many patients across large units. When emergencies arise—such as severe heart attacks (STEMI) combined with stroke—speed and coordination are essential.

Using smart glasses:

  • ICU staff stream live video and test results to attending physicians

  • Doctors evaluate patients remotely and in real time

  • Physicians guide treatment decisions, monitor vitals, and order immediate interventions

This eliminates delays caused by physical distance within the hospital and ensures faster clinical response.

Use Case 3: Surgical Collaboration

Surgery often requires consultation with specialists who may be off-site. Traditional solutions like smartphones fail due to poor angles, lighting, and obstruction.

With Vuzix Smart Glasses:

  • Surgeons broadcast full HD, first-person video during procedures

  • Remote specialists see exactly what the surgeon sees

  • Brightness, zoom, and clarity are optimized for surgical environments

  • Teams collaborate in real time without interrupting workflow

Surgeon Feedback

Dr. Bor-Chih Cheng, Chief of Cardiovascular Surgery at Chi Mei, used the glasses during a 16-hour surgery and reported:

“The Vuzix M400 Smart Glasses provided hands-free full HD video streaming for the entire operation. They allowed instant communication between the surgeon and ICU staff. The glasses are lightweight, easy to use, and let us treat patients while communicating seamlessly. We couldn’t be happier.”

Use Case 4: Training & Knowledge Sharing

Training junior physicians traditionally requires expensive recording setups and additional personnel. With Vuzix Smart Glasses:

  • Interns see procedures exactly as senior physicians perform them

  • Step-by-step guidance is delivered live

  • Questions and feedback happen in real time

  • Training can occur across locations

Applications include:

  • Symptom recognition

  • Suturing and wound care

  • Catheter implantation

  • Device operation and monitoring

This dramatically reduces training costs while improving learning quality.

Hands-Free Telemedicine & Conferencing

In urgent scenarios, staff can:

  1. Start a conference call from a phone

  2. Join instantly via smart glasses

  3. Share links with specialists across departments or hospitals

This “grab-and-go” usability ensures technology never slows care delivery.

Impact & Outcomes

By integrating Vuzix Smart Glasses, Chi Mei Medical Center achieved:

  • Faster diagnosis and treatment initiation

  • Improved collaboration across hospitals and departments

  • Reduced delays in emergency and ICU care

  • Enhanced surgical precision and consultation

  • More effective physician training and knowledge transfer

  • Better patient outcomes through earlier intervention

Looking Ahead

Chi Mei’s success demonstrates how wearable AR technology can fundamentally improve healthcare delivery. Rather than replacing human expertise, smart glasses amplify it—connecting clinicians to knowledge, specialists, and each other when it matters most.

As healthcare continues to evolve toward telemedicine, remote collaboration, and AI-supported care, Vuzix Smart Glasses are positioned as a foundational tool for modern clinical environments.

entry.title: Mutti, Vection & Vuzix
entry.content:
Digital Technical Assistance for Maintenance and Format Changeover

September 2021

Overview

The evolution of the Industry 4.0 paradigm has accelerated interest in applying digital technologies to industrial environments to optimize production processes. Among these technologies, augmented reality (AR) has emerged as a powerful tool.

This pilot project was launched to study, develop, and test an effective AR-based solution to support maintenance activities during in-line format changeover at Mutti. In Mutti’s industrial context, optimizing format changeover is strategically critical, as it represents a key point in production continuity and efficiency.

Mutti’s manufacturing process—spanning from raw material harvesting through processing and packaging—operates under strong seasonal pressure. Peak production periods demand maximum responsiveness to ensure product quality while maintaining high throughput. In this environment, speed, precision, and continuity during format changeovers are essential.

Project Partnership

At the end of 2020, Mutti and Vection Technologies began collaborating on a structured plan to test the application of augmented reality in industrial operations. The initiative was designed as a pilot project, serving as a test bed for the validation and adoption of digital technologies to support format changeover activities on production lines.

The project was promoted and supported by Mutti’s Industrial Direction, recognizing its strategic importance for long-term operational excellence.

Project Goals

The project had two primary goals:

  1. Optimize format changeover

    • Perform changeovers in the best possible way and as quickly as possible.

    • Maintain production continuity while improving accuracy and consistency.

  2. Enable knowledge sharing

    • Extend specialized competencies from a small group of experts to a broader pool of operators.

    • Ensure procedures could be executed by personnel who are not permanently assigned to a specific line.

The overarching objective was to share operational knowledge, allowing the company to manage competencies centrally, maximize efficiency, and maintain uninterrupted production capability.

Activities and Methodology

To achieve these goals, existing procedures had to be revised, completed, and fully digitized. This enabled their use through Vuzix M400 augmented reality smart glasses, allowing operators to access instructions directly in their field of view.

Project Phases

From a planning perspective, the project followed these steps:

  1. Assessment evaluation

  2. GANTT definition of the project

  3. Field testing with two format changeovers

  4. Pre-pilot

  5. Pilot

Assessment Evaluation

This phase focused on:

  • Awareness of project goals, available resources, and operator profiles

  • Analysis of existing procedures and how they were currently accessed

  • Evaluation of the proposed digital solution and new procedure formats

Procedure Redesign and Digitalization

Procedures were reformulated and enriched with:

  • Photographic documentation

  • Video recordings captured directly on the production line

  • Step-by-step breakdowns of all changeover phases

This content was digitized to enable hands-free access through AR smart glasses.

Field Testing & Pre-Pilot

Two real format changeovers were used to:

  • Validate procedure accuracy

  • Test usability of the AR interface

  • Gather operator feedback

A pre-pilot phase followed, consisting of a full day of stress testing and fine-tuning, both on the production line and in classroom settings.

The Pilot

The pilot took place on June 3, 2021, at Mutti’s Montechiarugolo plant.

For the first time, format changeover activities were performed by personnel not normally assigned to that production line, using only:

  • Digitized procedures

  • Vuzix M400 AR smart glasses

Operators carried out:

  • Disassembly

  • Retooling

  • Machine setup (depalletizer, filler, capper, labeler, shrink wrapper)

Key Operational Benefits

  • Operators followed certified Mutti procedures without diverting attention from their work.

  • Instructions were visible directly in the field of view.

  • Hands remained free, improving efficiency and safety.

  • A backend system enabled:

    • Operator log-on tracking

    • Monitoring of completed operations

    • Ongoing procedure updates and optimization

Key Results

Monitoring during the pilot produced unanimously positive results. The most significant outcomes included:

  1. Completion times comparable to expert personnel

  2. No issues during machine retooling

  3. Rapid learning of procedures

  4. Clear and intuitive instructions

  5. Continuous, on-site access to documentation

  6. Immediate familiarity with smart glasses

  7. Positive ergonomic evaluation and versatility of use

  8. Improved compliance with safety procedures

  9. Reduced need for dedicated changeover personnel

  10. Successful changeovers by non-specialized staff

  11. Fewer personnel movements between lines

  12. Full operational continuity throughout activities

  13. Initial skepticism toward digital tools was fully overcome by all involved personnel

Final Comments and Next Steps

The project delivered results that exceeded initial expectations.

Beyond functional success, the pilot demonstrated strong motivational and training benefits. Operators perceived the solution as a tool for professional growth rather than a replacement for experience.

The project confirmed that:

  • Technology enhances human expertise rather than replacing it

  • Knowledge can be standardized and shared effectively

  • AR solutions are viable for regular use in industrial format changeover

Future Outlook

Given the success of the pilot, Mutti and Vection plan to:

  • Extend the solution to additional lines and plants

  • Explore broader applications in industrial operations

  • Develop a structured roadmap for adopting augmented and virtual reality technologies across business processes

Acknowledgments

This project was made possible through strong collaboration, trust, and team spirit between Mutti and Vection. The commitment to innovation and the willingness to test new technologies played a key role in turning the initial vision into a successful reality.
